column1: Which opposition governors did the Supreme Court uphold in January 2024?
column2: Abba Yusuf (NNPP, Kano), Caleb Mutfwang (PDP, Plateau), Alex Otti (LP, Abia), Bala Mohammed (PDP, Bauchi) and Dauda Lawal (PDP, Zamfara).

column1: How does the January 2024 Supreme Court ruling counter "the courts only favour the APC"?
column2: The court overturned lower-court rulings that had sacked five opposition governors, letting voters keep the governors they elected.

column1: What did PLAC's audit of 2023 election petitions find?
column2: Of 1,209 petitions (1,003 pursued after 206 withdrawals), 88.9% failed at tribunals and 79.4% at the Court of Appeal, showing courts largely upheld the polling-unit results.

column1: What is the Judicial Office Holders' Salaries and Allowances Act 2024?
column2: A law Tinubu signed in August 2024 raising judicial salaries, allowances and retirement benefits by 300%, the first review since 2007.

column1: How much do the Chief Justice and Supreme Court Justices earn under the 2024 salary law?
column2: The CJN earns ₦64 million a year and Supreme Court Justices ₦61.4 million.

column1: Why is the judicial pay rise used to counter "judges are bribed"?
column2: Better-paid judges are less financially vulnerable to inducement, strengthening judicial independence.

column1: Who is the Chief Justice of Nigeria cited in the playbook?
column2: Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, who enforces NJC discipline and has warned against conflicting ex-parte orders ahead of 2027.

column1: What did the Supreme Court decide on local government autonomy in July 2024?
column2: In a suit filed by the Federal Government, it affirmed direct financial autonomy for all 774 LGAs and ruled that governors cannot unilaterally dissolve elected councils.

column1: How does local government autonomy benefit ordinary citizens?
column2: Funds for local schools, clinics, roads and security go directly to elected councils instead of being held in state joint accounts.

column1: What voter register clean-up did INEC carry out ahead of 2027?
column2: It expunged 1.6 million irregular and duplicate records across 10 states and flagged 54 officials for sanctions.

column1: How many judges have been nominated for the 2027 election tribunals?
What is the difference between IReV and statutory result collation?
column2: The Supreme Court held IReV is a public viewing portal for transparency, distinct from legal collation; the Electoral Act 2026 further codified electronic transmission.

column1: Give examples of connectivity projects addressing rural result-upload problems.
column2: Project 774 LG Net, 4,000 approved USPF rural telecom towers and NigComSat-1R satellite broadband for off-grid communities.

column1: How are INEC commissioners vetted under Section 154 of the Constitution?
column2: Nominees are checked by security agencies, reviewed by the Council of State and confirmed through public Senate screening.

column1: How has the NIN database strengthened election and welfare administration?
column2: NIMC expanded it past 100 million records and harmonised NIN with SIM data, removing ghost beneficiaries and improving identity checks.

column1: Why do opposition narratives about the courts and INEC matter before 2027?
column2: The playbook says they aim to depress turnout, frame institutions as compromised and erase reforms made since May 2023.

column1: How should a caller answer "Why vote when courts hand victories to the ruling party?"
column2: Acknowledge the frustration, then cite the five opposition governors upheld in 2024 and LG autonomy; your vote at the polling unit still decides who governs.
